A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CROWDNOTES+ research and contain 20 complete, readable pages, including Appendices A–F. Full text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v3 reports original analysis of 30,791 health-related Community Notes, experiments with 15 LLM configurations on HEALTHNOTES, ablations, and human evaluations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical studies, including the benchmark experiments, human preference results, and appendix evaluations of judge reliability.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–D retain identical augmentation, automation, evidence-selection, and hierarchical evaluation procedures, including HEALTHJUDGE training.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English health-note corpus, 1,268-pair HEALTHNOTES benchmark, and augmentation and automation scenarios. No dataset, domain, or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same Human Baseline and 15 LLM configurations. The helpfulness-judge comparators in Table 7 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings, splits, retrieval controls, and character limits are identical. Appendix D.4.2 retains 100 correctness judgments, balanced 50/50 across subsets, assessed by the same three annotators.

E4.justification: The ablations, error analyses, human preference study, and workflow case studies are unchanged. Appendix D.4.2 revises a validation outcome without documenting any change to the analysis performed.

E5.justification: Appendix E.2 retains single-run reporting, and Appendix D.4 retains majority-vote agreement reporting. The changed agreement count is a result revision, not a change in statistical or uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Appendix D.4.2, page 17, changes GPT-4.1 correctness-judge agreement with aggregated human judgments from 97/100 to 99/100 under unchanged reported settings. All other numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and formulations, including the hierarchical probability decomposition in Equation 1, are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about governance delays, CROWDNOTES+, HEALTHNOTES, crowd-rating weaknesses, and LLM-generated note quality.

C2.justification: Appendix D.4.2 retains its strong-alignment and sanity-check interpretation despite the revised count. The discussion, limitations, ethical considerations, and Appendix A interpretations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Prompts, preprocessing, training hyperparameters, model versions, and code/data access statements are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to earlier research are identical.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3, 22 Apr 2026, to v4, 1 Jun 2026. Apart from the numerical revision in Appendix D.4.2, prose, terminology, and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–11, Tables 1–9, captions, placement, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered differences are confined to the version/date stamp and one numeral in running text.

improvement.justification: The only substantive revision raises reported correctness-judge agreement from 97/100 to 99/100. Both versions already interpret this validation as strong alignment, and no additional validation or explanation accompanies the revision. With methods, main results, reproducibility information, and substantive exposition otherwise identical, the higher reported agreement does not establish a meaningful overall quality improvement.
